steps.title: Energy conservation, integral form
steps.why: Start from conservation of energy for a fixed control volume $V$ in the pore space. Energy changes only through the flux across its boundary, because there are no external heat sources.

check.printed: This is a postulate (first law for an open control volume, with pressure work neglected per A4), so no tool can check it.

steps.title: Local form
steps.why: Apply the divergence theorem. Because $V$ is arbitrary and the fields are smooth (A1), the integrand must vanish pointwise.

check.printed: Standard localization argument; no symbolic content to check.

steps.title: Energy density and mass balances
steps.why: Write the energy per volume as ice (fraction $\phi$) plus vapor in the gas (fraction $1-\phi$), each at the local $T$. Ice mass is lost at rate $\dot m$, which becomes vapor. Ice does not move.
steps.operation: definition of e; mass balances for ice and vapor

check.printed: Definitions and modeling assumptions; their use is checked in check_s4.

steps.title: Expand and use the mass balances
steps.why: Apply the product rule to $\partial_t e$ and $\nabla\cdot(h_v\mathbf{j}_v)$, then substitute the two mass balances of S3. The terms with $h_v\nabla\cdot\mathbf{j}_v$ cancel, and the enthalpy difference multiplies $\dot m$.
steps.latex: \left[\phi\rho_i c_i + (1-\phi)\rho_v c_v\right]\partial_t T + \dot m\left(h_v - h_i\right) + c_v\,\mathbf{j}_v\cdot\nabla T + \nabla\cdot\mathbf{q} = 0

check.printed: product rule ok: True; mass-balance substitution ok: True

steps.title: Constitutive closures
steps.why: Define the latent heat and the mixture heat capacity. Use Fourier's law for conduction with a conductivity that depends on phase and temperature. Express $\dot m$ through $\phi$, which needs constant $\rho_i$ (A5).
steps.latex: L_{sub}(T) = h_v - h_i,\quad C(\phi,T) = \phi\rho_i c_i + (1-\phi)\rho_v c_v,\quad \mathbf{q} = -k(\phi,T)\nabla T,\quad \dot m = -\rho_i\,\partial_t\phi

check.printed: Definitions; $\dot m$ follows from S3 with $\partial_t\rho_i=0$.

steps.title: Drop vapor enthalpy advection
steps.why: The term $c_v\mathbf{j}_v\cdot\nabla T$ is the heat carried by diffusing vapor. It is many orders of magnitude smaller than conduction (see neglected), so drop it.

steps.title: Heat equation with latent heat, residual form
steps.why: Substitute the closures of S5 and write the divergence in 3D Cartesian coordinates. Deposition ($\partial_t\phi>0$) releases heat and raises $T$; sublimation absorbs it. Every term is in W m$^{-3}$.
steps.latex: R = C(\phi,T)\partial_t T - \partial_x(k\,\partial_x T) - \partial_y(k\,\partial_y T) - \partial_z(k\,\partial_z T) - \rho_i L_{sub}(T)\,\partial_t\phi = 0

check.printed: C T_t 1400000.0 watt / meter ** 3; div k grad T 3.5 watt / meter ** 3; rho L phi_t 2567600000.0 watt / meter ** 3 (all terms in W/m^3)

assumptions_used: A1: $\phi(x,y,z,t)$ is a known, smooth field (given), and $T$ is smooth.
A2: There are no external heat sources (no radiation absorbed in the pore volume, no Joule heating).
A3: Ice and gas share one local temperature $T$ in the diffuse interface (local thermal equilibrium).
A4: Pressure work and kinetic energy are negligible, so internal energy and enthalpy are interchangeable.
A5: The ice is rigid and at rest, with constant density $\rho_i$, so $\dot m = -\rho_i\partial_t\phi$.
A6: The gas is water vapor only (any inert gas is negligible in the lunar pore space); it moves only by diffusion with flux $\mathbf{j}_v$, and there is no bulk gas flow.
A7: Heat conduction follows Fourier's law $\mathbf{q}=-k(\phi,T)\nabla T$ with an isotropic conductivity.
A8: The heat carried by diffusing vapor, $c_v\mathbf{j}_v\cdot\nabla T$, is negligible next to conduction.

neglected.effect: Heat carried by diffusing vapor, $c_v\mathbf{j}_v\cdot\nabla T$
neglected.why: $|\mathbf{j}_v|\sim D\rho_v/\ell \sim 10^{-5}\cdot10^{-7}/10^{-5}\approx10^{-7}$ kg m$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$, so $c_v|\mathbf{j}_v|\sim2\times10^{-4}$ W m$^{-2}$ K$^{-1}$, against $k/\ell\sim3.5/10^{-5}\approx3\times10^5$ W m$^{-2}$ K$^{-1}$: a ratio near $10^{-9}$.

neglected.effect: Sensible heat of the vapor inside $C$
neglected.why: It is kept formally, but $(1-\phi)\rho_v c_v\sim10^{-4}$ J m$^{-3}$ K$^{-1}$ against $\rho_i c_i\sim1.4\times10^6$, so $C\approx\phi\rho_i c_i$ in practice.

neglected.effect: Inert gas (air) and its enthalpy transport
neglected.why: Lunar pore gas is near vacuum, so its heat capacity and its enthalpy flux are negligible. A model with air would add $(1-\phi)\rho_a c_a$ to $C$ and an air-flux term like the one above.
Gas pressures are tiny (vapor pressure around 1e-3 Pa at 200 K) and nothing flows fast, so $p\,dV$ work is many orders of magnitude below the latent heat.

$4\epsilon\sigma T^3\ell\sim4\cdot5.7\times10^{-8}\cdot8\times10^6\cdot10^{-4}\approx2\times10^{-4}$ W m$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$ effective conductivity at 200 K and 100 $\mu$m pores, small next to ice $k\approx3.5$. It is excluded under A2.

neglected.effect: Interface (surface) energy and curvature effect on latent heat
neglected.why: Capillary energy $\gamma/\ell\sim0.1/10^{-5}=10^4$ J m$^{-3}$ is much less than $\rho_i L_{sub}\approx2.6\times10^9$ J m$^{-3}$.

neglected.effect: Density change of ice with temperature (thermal expansion)
neglected.why: The volumetric expansion coefficient of ice is about $1.5\times10^{-4}$ K$^{-1}$, so $\rho_i$ changes by under 1% over tens of kelvin. Constant $\rho_i$ is needed in S5 to write $\dot m=-\rho_i\partial_t\phi$.

neglected.effect: Regolith grains (solid silicate) in the energy balance
neglected.why: The task models only the pore space (ice + gas). The grains enter through boundary conditions, not through this equation.
